newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH ELBREWERY'S BEER SALES UP IN 1996.
newsitem.headline: POLISH ELBREWERY'S BEER SALES UP IN 1996.

text.p: Poland's largest brewery, Elbrewery Company Ltd, owned by Australia's Brewpole BV, increased its beer sales by 100,000 hectolitres to 2.66 million hectolitres last year, the brewery president said on Thursday.
Czeslaw Debski told a news conference that the increase had allowed the company to remain the market leader, although its market share shrank by one point to 16 percent.
He blamed bad marketing decisions and a cold summer season for the market share decline.
"We are going to defend our market leader position through attack. We plan to strengthen our promotion and marketing," he said, adding that spending on marketing would grow by one-third in 1997.
He declined to give financial results for 1996, saying only that gross and operating profit increased.

Debski said the company would introduce new brands of beer this year and consolidate the operations of Elbrewery and Brewpole's other Polish subsidiary, Hevelius Brewing Co, which will function as a group named the EB Group.
He said the group, with output capacity of 4.3 million hectolitres, wanted to sell 3.7 million hectolitres in 1997.
Brewpole is owned by a group of Australian investors and Dutch brewer Royal Grolsch NV , which has a 25 percent stake.
